prompt: Design a personal running coach app — a home dashboard with this week's training plan, run streaks, and weekly mileage stats, and a workout detail page showing pace, splits, elevation, and coach notes for a single run. Make it feel motivating, clean, and athletic.
title: Pace

issues.description: The mount audit requires RunStatusSummary, but detail.jsx does not import or render RunStatusSummary. The verified file instead imports Avatar, Badge, Button, Card, CoachNotesPanel, ElevationSummary, and RunSplitsTable. This leaves the required run-status/page-header component absent from the detail workflow.

The primary home CTA is rendered as <Button size="lg">{copy.primaryCta}</Button> with no onClick, href, or form behavior. The brief requires a clear start or resume action for the next run, so “Start shakeout” is visibly presented but functionally inert.

The measured detail screen reports that Archivo is not loaded. detail.jsx adds an external Google Fonts link, which is not a reliable self-contained font source and does not guarantee the company’s condensed display type. This weakens the required Nike-style headline and scoreboard hierarchy.

The measured home screen also reports that Archivo is not loaded. The hero headline uses var(--font-display, var(--font-body)), so it falls back to the body font when the display token is unavailable, losing the required bold condensed athletic voice.

The component uses --accent-foreground for text and icon color, but the supplied design tokens define --accent without defining --accent-foreground. The same undefined-token pattern appears in Badge.jsx and Button.jsx for other foreground tokens, creating unreliable text contrast and token violations on interactive surfaces.

The detail layout plan calls for five custom sections with the card surface after the rows pane and CTA band. The verified screen imports the generic Card wrapper alongside multiple detail components, making the detail likely read as a stack of repeated outlined panels. This exceeds the scarce-card guidance and competes with the single-run chart/detail moment; use divided rows or tonal bands for secondary data.

The loading state uses animate-pulse placeholders, but the component contains no prefers-reduced-motion handling. The universal law requires motion behavior to be reduced or disabled for users who request reduced motion.
The geometry gate measured 2 of 15 detail elements off the 8px grid. Without changing the measured result, align those specific elements to the shared spacing and inset tokens in detail.jsx.

The required pace chart is visually empty: the large chart panel contains only a baseline, a single '1km' marker, and a 0.0–0.0 range. This fails the single-run detail intent to explain pace over time using the completed run's actual data.

RunSplitsTable renders column headers but only shows 'No splits available', while the summary above lists splits from 1 km through 9 km. The required split table is therefore visibly incomplete and contradicts the same run's summary.
The RunStatusSummary reports 64 m elevation gain, but ElevationSummary displays 0 m. The focused detail screen must present one internally consistent run record.

The home screen shows only the next 'Easy shakeout' workout. The required remaining weekly training plan and its dated sequence are not visible, so the primary coaching-dashboard workflow is incomplete.

The scoreboard says Run Streak is 9 days and Weekly Consistency is 75%, but the visible StreakProgress rings independently display 0d and 0%. This makes the core streak component appear broken and undermines trust in the dashboard.

The brief requires current consecutive-run streak, longest streak, and weekly consistency. Current streak and consistency appear as separate values, but no longest-streak value is visible anywhere on the screen.

Two visually prominent start actions compete at the top and inside the workout panel: 'Start shakeout' and 'Start workout'. The coaching dashboard should establish one clear primary action for the next run.

There is an unusually large, mostly empty vertical gap between the scoreboard/rings area and the next-workout panel. The whitespace does not create a deliberate accent band or content transition and makes the dashboard feel unfinished rather than balanced.

The detail screen is predominantly white with thin gray borders and green status accents, but lacks the Nike language's distinctive volt accent, scoreboard energy, and bold athletic hierarchy. The chart and metrics should provide a stronger branded performance moment without adding decorative clutter.
Archivo is reported as not loaded, and the primary heading reads as a generic broad sans rather than the required condensed, heavy display treatment. This weakens hierarchy and brand fidelity.
Archivo is reported as not loaded on the dashboard as well. The large mileage headline should be the strongest condensed scoreboard moment on the screen, but the current type treatment feels generic.

reviewResult.summary: The screens use relevant running data and generally follow the track-mode direction, with strong concrete copy and a credible scoreboard/detail concept. Approval is blocked by the missing required RunStatusSummary component, an inert primary home action, unreliable display-font loading, and undefined foreground tokens that can compromise contrast. Detail also needs tighter surface discipline and reduced-motion handling.
requiredFixes: Mount RunStatusSummary in src/screens/detail.jsx so the required run status/page header component visibly renders the completed state, metrics, and pace chart.
Wire the primary Start shakeout action in src/screens/home.jsx to a real workout-start or resume interaction, with an accessible state change.
Load Archivo reliably for both verified screens through the shared theme/font setup, and remove reliance on an external font link that can fail at runtime.
Replace undefined foreground tokens such as --accent-foreground, --secondary-foreground, --card-foreground, and --destructive-foreground with defined theme tokens.
Reduce repeated Card surfaces in src/screens/detail.jsx and alternate the chart, split rows, elevation, and coach-note sections with distinct justified surfaces.
Align the two off-grid elements measured on detail to the 8px layout grid.
detail: Populate the pace-over-time chart with the selected run's actual pace data, axes, units, and readable labels instead of rendering an empty plot with 0.0–0.0.
detail: Render the run's kilometer split rows in RunSplitsTable; do not show 'No splits available' when split data is already displayed in the summary.
detail: Make ElevationSummary use the selected run's actual 64 m elevation gain rather than displaying 0 m.
home: Fix StreakProgress so its rings reflect the adjacent 9-day streak and 75% consistency values, and add the required longest-streak metric.
home: Render the complete dated weekly training plan after the next-workout cue, including remaining workout types, distances, target paces, completion states, and start/resume actions.
home: Consolidate the top 'Start shakeout' and card-level 'Start workout' controls into one clear primary action, with the secondary entry point made quiet.
detail and home: Load Archivo through the design tokens and use the condensed, heavy type treatment required by the Nike design language.
